compliance_note: No target variable was selected or proposed in this phase; no model was trained.

insights.question: What is the overall churn rate, and how does it vary by contract type?
insights.business_relevance: Contract structure is the company's main retention lever: it defines exit cost and repeat decision points for every customer.
insights.interpretation: Overall churn is 26.5% (1,869/7,043). Contract commitment dominates: month-to-month customers churn at 42.7% - 15.1x the 2.8% rate of two-year customers - and although they are 55% of the base they carry ~87% of churned monthly revenue ($120.8K of $139.1K). The least-committed segment is also the most expensive per month.
insights.recommended_action: Launch a contract-migration program: incentivize month-to-month customers (3,875 accounts) to move to 1-2 year terms via lock-in discounts and bundles; track churn-by-contract monthly.

insights.question: How does churn risk change across the customer lifecycle (tenure)?
insights.business_relevance: If risk concentrates in the first year, onboarding is the highest-leverage operational process for retention.
insights.interpretation: Risk decays monotonically with tenure: 52.2% in the first 6 months vs 6.4% after five years (~8x gradient). Half of all churned customers left with <= 10 months of tenure; 613 customers sit at exactly 1 month - the onboarding cliff.
insights.recommended_action: Stand up a 90-day onboarding program (proactive setup call, first-invoice check, expectation management) with cohort survival at months 3 and 6 as its KPI.

insights.question: How does churn differ by internet service type, and do value-added add-ons protect against churn?
insights.business_relevance: The flagship premium product is leaking at double the rate of the legacy one - a product-level warning with direct revenue consequences.
insights.interpretation: Fiber churns at 41.9% vs 19.0% for DSL despite being the premium product ($91.68 vs $56.15 median charge). Add-ons correlate inversely with churn: without OnlineSecurity/TechSupport churn is ~33-42%; with both, 9.0%. Plausible mechanisms: bundling stickiness and/or selection (unhappy fiber customers buy fewer add-ons). Either way, unprotected fiber customers are the red zone.
insights.recommended_action: 1) Investigate fiber service quality (installation, outages, expectation gap). 2) Bundle OnlineSecurity + TechSupport into fiber onboarding at promotional price. 3) Track the protected-vs-unprotected churn gap as a leading indicator.

insights.question: How much monthly recurring revenue is at risk from churn, and how is that risk distributed across price bands?
insights.business_relevance: Churn must be managed in dollars: revenue at risk, not customer counts, is what leadership can act on.
insights.interpretation: Churners are worth more than stayers: ARPU $74.44 vs $61.27 (+21.5%). As a result 30.5% of all MRR ($139.1K/mo, $1.67M annualized) sits in churned accounts - far above their 26.5% customer share. The $70-95 band alone concentrates 50.2% of at-risk revenue with a 37.1% churn rate.
insights.recommended_action: 1) Make retention budget revenue-weighted: prioritize $70+ accounts. 2) Audit the $95+ premium bundle's price-value gap. 3) Report 'monthly revenue at risk' as the primary KPI next to churn count.

insights.question: How does churn differ by payment method and paperless billing, and is there a compounding effect?
insights.business_relevance: Payment behavior is a cheap, testable lever: it can be changed with a small incentive without touching the product.
insights.interpretation: Manual payment correlates with churn: electronic check churns at 45.3% vs 15-17% for automatic methods (~3x). Paperless billing shows the same direction (33.6% vs 16.3%), and they compound: e-check + paperless is the leakiest configuration at 49.8%. Mechanism hypothesis: manual payment creates a monthly re-authorization decision point; automatic payment removes it. Correlation, not proven causation - payment type also proxies for customer profile.
insights.recommended_action: Run an A/B-tested payment-migration campaign (incentivize e-check customers to switch to automatic payments), prioritizing e-check + paperless accounts. E-check churned MRR is $84.3K/mo.

synthesis.what_happened: 26.5% of the base churns, taking 30.5% of monthly revenue ($139K/mo; $1.67M annualized) with it. Churn concentrates in month-to-month contracts, the first year of tenure, fiber-optic users without protection add-ons, and manual-payment customers.
synthesis.why_it_happened: The data shows structural exit-cost asymmetry (contract), lifecycle fragility (tenure spike at month 1), a price/expectation gap in the premium product (fiber), and monthly re-authorization friction (manual payment). These four mechanisms compound in overlapping segments.
synthesis.what_to_do: Four levers, in priority order: (1) contract migration for month-to-month accounts; (2) 90-day onboarding program for new customers; (3) fiber quality investigation + protection bundling; (4) A/B-tested migration from electronic check to automatic payments. Weight retention spend by monthly revenue at risk, not by customer count.
